Consult Summary:
- 58-year-old woman with 5-day history of dry cough and profuse nasal discharge, no red-flag respiratory features, assessed via telehealth.
- Impression of viral upper respiratory tract infection; advised symptomatic care, temperature monitoring and safety-netting due to diabetes.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute upper respiratory tract infection / dry cough (5 days)
- Symptoms: dry cough every 20–30 min, green nasal discharge, subjective fevers with alternating chills, myalgia; no sputum, no chest pain, no dyspnoea, no haemoptysis, no sore throat/ear pain, no rash, vision change or headache.
- Systems review: GI—transient diarrhoea at onset, resolved; GU—normal urine output, no frequency or thirst.
- Examination: none performed (teleconsult); no vitals provided.
- Clinical impression: likely viral infection; bacterial superinfection risk increased due to diabetes.

Issue 2: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (pre-existing)
- On metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Last blood test 3 weeks ago reported “normal”.
- No home blood-glucose monitoring equipment; weight 65 kg, height 5′5″.

Issue 3: Hypertension (pre-existing)
- On lisinopril “200” (dose/route/frequency not documented; dose appears high—conflict noted).
- Last BP check “a while ago”; stability uncertain.

Medications:
- Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Lisinopril – “200” (dose/route/frequency not documented; patient-reported value).
- Lemsip (paracetamol-containing cold remedy) – 2–3 sachets daily as needed.

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies; reports mild seasonal hay fever.

Past Medical History:
- Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Hypertension.

Social History:
- Lives with partner and dog.
- Occupation: office manager.
- Alcohol: “odd sherry” (occasional).
- Smoking history: not documented.

Preventative History:
- Routine diabetes and blood-pressure reviews advised; dates not provided.
- No information on other screening tests or vaccinations.

Physical Examination:
- None performed; no vital signs recorded (telehealth).

Plan:
- Obtain a thermometer; monitor temperature regularly.
- Continue symptomatic relief with Lemsip; avoid additional paracetamol-containing products.
- Daytime: avoid cough suppressants; may use small amount at night if cough prevents sleep.
- Red-flags requiring re-assessment: temperature >37.5–38 °C persisting or rising, worsening cough, development of purulent sputum, haemoptysis, epistaxis, dyspnoea, or chest pain.
- If deterioration occurs, consider in-person review and possible antibiotics.
- Ensure routine diabetes and hypertension follow-up with GP, including BP measurement and blood tests.
- No immediate prescription issued.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: objective vitals, physical examination, smoking status, full medication doses/routes/frequencies, formal allergy list.
● Internal conflicts: Lisinopril reported as “200” (unusually high dose).
● Transcript quality: clear; minor pauses, no major inaudible sections.
